recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-12468; future reviews should treat FHIR-12842 and the CodeableReference migration as the current interpretation of the original alignment request.
issue_request: FHIR-12468 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy change request for DSTU2 asking MedicationAdministration to mirror MedicationStatement by renaming reasonGiven to reasonGivenCodeableConcept, renaming reasonReference to reasonGivenReference, and ordering the given-reason elements together after not-given elements.
initial_application: Git-svn commit 805a87d6445447d15f8df95750cdebdf698056e5 applied the seed by renaming MedicationAdministration reasonGiven/reasonReference fields and changing their order. Later Published Pharmacy issue FHIR-12842, applied by 3e6ab010725e97201494594d25960f3a4ebbb7df, intentionally harmonized those intermediate names to reasonCode and reasonReference across pharmacy resources.
additional_context: MedicationAdministration is active in source/fhir.ini. Current R5/R6 source has a single MedicationAdministration.reason CodeableReference with Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, and Procedure reference targets, and fhir.ini records the migration from reasonCode/reasonReference into reason.concept/reason.reference. MedicationStatement.reason uses the same CodeableReference pattern, so later modeling preserves the requested alignment even though the literal DSTU2-era names are gone.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. Restoring reasonGivenCodeableConcept or reasonGivenReference would contradict the later Pharmacy harmonization and the current CodeableReference model; the active source already supports coded and referenced administration reasons in the aligned current form.

related_jiras.note: Published Pharmacy harmonization changed MedicationAdministration reasonGivenCodeableConcept/reasonGivenReference to the broader reasonCode/reasonReference pattern after FHIR-12468 was applied.
